1//! ONNX embedding provider implementation using tract.
2//!
3//! This module provides embedding generation using ONNX models via the tract runtime.
4//! The default model is `0dinai/0din-jailbreak-embeddings-small` which produces 1024-dimensional embeddings.
5//!
6//! ## Features
7//!
8//! - Local ONNX model inference (no API calls)
9//! - Automatic model download from HuggingFace
10//! - Mean pooling with attention masking
11//! - L2 normalization of embeddings
12//! - Support for E5 models with "query: " prefix
13//!
14//! ## Usage
15//!
16//! Enable the `onnx` feature in your `Cargo.toml`:
17//!
18//! ```toml
19//! signature-sdk = { version = "0.1", features = ["onnx"] }
20//! ```
21//!
22//! ## Example
23//!
24//! ```no_run
25//! # #[cfg(feature = "onnx")]
26//! # async fn example() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
27//! use odin_prompt_toolkit::providers::{OnnxProvider, ModelCache};
28//! use odin_prompt_toolkit::provider::EmbeddingProvider;
29//!
30//! let cache = ModelCache::new()?;
31//! let provider = OnnxProvider::new(&cache, None, None).await?;
32//!
33//! let result = provider.generate_embedding("Hello, world!").await?;
34//! println!("Embedding dimensions: {}", result.embedding.len());
35//! # Ok(())
36//! # }
37//! ```
38
39use async_trait::async_trait;
40use std::sync::Arc;
41use tracing::{debug, info};
42use tract_ndarray::Array2;
43use tract_onnx::prelude::*;
44
45use crate::error::{SigError, Result};
46use crate::lsh::{compute_embedding_sha256, normalize_vector};
47use crate::provider::EmbeddingProvider;
48use crate::providers::ModelCache;
49use crate::types::EmbeddingResult;
50
51/// Type alias for the tract ONNX inference plan to reduce complexity
52type TractModel = SimplePlan<TypedFact, Box<dyn TypedOp>, Graph<TypedFact, Box<dyn TypedOp>>>;
53
54/// ONNX embedding provider using tract runtime.
55///
56/// This provider uses the `0dinai/0din-jailbreak-embeddings-small` model by default,
57/// which produces 1024-dimensional embeddings suitable for multilingual text similarity.
58///
59/// The model is automatically downloaded from HuggingFace on first use and cached locally.
60#[derive(Debug)]
61pub struct OnnxProvider {
62    /// Tract inference plan
63    model: Arc<TractModel>,
64
65    /// Tokenizer for text preprocessing
66    tokenizer: Arc<tokenizers::Tokenizer>,
67
68    /// Model name (HuggingFace ID or local path)
69    model_name: String,
70
71    /// Embedding dimensions
72    dimensions: usize,
73
74    /// Provider name
75    name: String,
76
77    /// Input prefix (e.g., "query: " for E5 models, empty for others)
78    input_prefix: String,
79}
80
81impl OnnxProvider {
82    /// Default model for ONNX embeddings.
83    pub const DEFAULT_MODEL: &'static str = "models/v1";
84
85    /// Default embedding dimensions.
86    pub const DEFAULT_DIMENSIONS: usize = 1024;
87
88    /// Maximum sequence length supported by the model.
89    pub const MAX_SEQUENCE_LENGTH: usize = 512;
90
91    /// Input prefix required by E5 models.
92    pub const INPUT_PREFIX: &'static str = "query: ";
93
94    /// ONNX model filenames (prefer optimized, fall back to unoptimized).
95    const ONNX_MODEL_FILE_OPTIMIZED: &'static str = "onnx/model_O4.onnx";
96    const ONNX_MODEL_FILE_UNOPTIMIZED: &'static str = "onnx/model.onnx";
97
98    /// Create a new ONNX provider.
99    ///
100    /// # Arguments
101    ///
102    /// * `cache` - Model cache for downloading/caching models
103    /// * `model` - Model name or HuggingFace ID (default: intfloat/multilingual-e5-small)
104    /// * `name` - Provider name identifier (default: "onnx")
105    ///
106    /// # Errors
107    ///
108    /// Returns an error if:
109    /// - Model download fails
110    /// - ONNX model loading fails
111    /// - Tokenizer loading fails
112    pub async fn new(
113        cache: &ModelCache,
114        model: Option<String>,
115        name: Option<String>,
116    ) -> Result<Self> {
117        let model_name = model.unwrap_or_else(|| Self::DEFAULT_MODEL.to_string());
118        let provider_name = name.unwrap_or_else(|| "onnx".to_string());
119
120        info!("Initializing ONNX provider with model: {}", model_name);
121
122        // Try optimized model first, fall back to unoptimized
123        let model_path = match cache.get_model(&model_name, Self::ONNX_MODEL_FILE_OPTIMIZED).await {
124            Ok(path) => {
125                debug!("Using optimized ONNX model (model_O4.onnx)");
126                path
127            }
128            Err(_) => {
129                debug!("Optimized model not found, trying unoptimized (model.onnx)");
130                cache.get_model(&model_name, Self::ONNX_MODEL_FILE_UNOPTIMIZED).await?
131            }
132        };
133        let tokenizer_path = cache.get_tokenizer(&model_name).await?;
134
135        info!("Loading ONNX model from: {}", model_path.display());
136
137        // Load ONNX model with tract
138        let model = tract_onnx::onnx()
139            .model_for_path(&model_path)
140            .map_err(|e| SigError::Provider(format!("Failed to load ONNX model: {}", e)))?
141            .into_optimized()
142            .map_err(|e| SigError::Provider(format!("Failed to optimize ONNX model: {}", e)))?
143            .into_runnable()
144            .map_err(|e| {
145                SigError::Provider(format!("Failed to create runnable model: {}", e))
146            })?;
147
148        info!("ONNX model loaded successfully");
149
150        // Load tokenizer
151        info!("Loading tokenizer from: {}", tokenizer_path.display());
152        let tokenizer = tokenizers::Tokenizer::from_file(&tokenizer_path)
153            .map_err(|e| SigError::Provider(format!("Failed to load tokenizer: {}", e)))?;
154
155        info!("Tokenizer loaded successfully");
156
157        // Detect input prefix from model configuration
158        let input_prefix = Self::detect_input_prefix(&model_name, cache)
159            .await
160            .unwrap_or_else(|e| {
161                debug!(
162                    "Could not detect input prefix from config, using default: {}",
163                    e
164                );
165                Self::INPUT_PREFIX.to_string()
166            });
167
168        if input_prefix.is_empty() {
169            info!("Model does not require input prefix");
170        } else {
171            info!("Using input prefix: {:?}", input_prefix);
172        }
173
174        Ok(Self {
175            model: Arc::new(model),
176            tokenizer: Arc::new(tokenizer),
177            model_name,
178            dimensions: Self::DEFAULT_DIMENSIONS,
179            name: provider_name,
180            input_prefix,
181        })
182    }
183
184    /// Detect input prefix from model's sentence_transformers config.
185    ///
186    /// Returns empty string if no prefix is needed (custom models).
187    /// Returns "query: " or similar if the model config specifies a prompt.
188    /// Falls back to default E5 prefix on error.
189    async fn detect_input_prefix(model_id: &str, cache: &ModelCache) -> Result<String> {
190        // Try to load the sentence_transformers config
191        let config_path = cache
192            .get_model(model_id, "config_sentence_transformers.json")
193            .await?;
194
195        let config_str = tokio::fs::read_to_string(&config_path).await.map_err(|e| {
196            SigError::Provider(format!("Failed to read sentence_transformers config: {}", e))
197        })?;
198
199        let config: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&config_str).map_err(|e| {
200            SigError::Provider(format!("Failed to parse sentence_transformers config: {}", e))
201        })?;
202
203        // Check if prompts.query is non-empty
204        if let Some(query_prompt) = config
205            .get("prompts")
206            .and_then(|p| p.get("query"))
207            .and_then(|q| q.as_str())
208        {
209            if !query_prompt.is_empty() {
210                // E5 models use "query: " with trailing space
211                return Ok(format!("{} ", query_prompt));
212            }
213        }
214
215        // No prefix needed (custom model case)
216        Ok(String::new())
217    }
218
219    /// Tokenize text and prepare inputs for the model.
220    ///
221    /// This method:
222    /// 1. Prepends the input prefix if configured (e.g., "query: " for E5 models)
223    /// 2. Tokenizes the text
224    /// 3. Truncates to max sequence length
225    /// 4. Returns input IDs and attention mask
226    fn tokenize(&self, text: &str) -> Result<(Vec<i64>, Vec<i64>)> {
227        // Prepend prefix if configured
228        let prefixed_text = if self.input_prefix.is_empty() {
229            text.to_string()
230        } else {
231            format!("{}{}", self.input_prefix, text)
232        };
233
234        // Tokenize
235        let encoding = self
236            .tokenizer
237            .encode(prefixed_text, true)
238            .map_err(|e| SigError::Provider(format!("Tokenization failed: {}", e)))?;
239
240        // Get token IDs and attention mask
241        let mut input_ids: Vec<i64> = encoding.get_ids().iter().map(|&id| id as i64).collect();
242        let mut attention_mask: Vec<i64> = encoding
243            .get_attention_mask()
244            .iter()
245            .map(|&m| m as i64)
246            .collect();
247
248        // Truncate to max sequence length
249        if input_ids.len() > Self::MAX_SEQUENCE_LENGTH {
250            debug!(
251                "Truncating sequence from {} to {} tokens",
252                input_ids.len(),
253                Self::MAX_SEQUENCE_LENGTH
254            );
255            input_ids.truncate(Self::MAX_SEQUENCE_LENGTH);
256            attention_mask.truncate(Self::MAX_SEQUENCE_LENGTH);
257        }
258
259        Ok((input_ids, attention_mask))
260    }
261
262    /// Run inference on the ONNX model.
263    ///
264    /// # Arguments
265    ///
266    /// * `input_ids` - Token IDs
267    /// * `attention_mask` - Attention mask
268    ///
269    /// # Returns
270    ///
271    /// Raw token embeddings from the model (before pooling).
272    fn run_inference(&self, input_ids: &[i64], attention_mask: &[i64]) -> Result<Array2<f32>> {
273        let seq_len = input_ids.len();
274
275        // Create input tensors
276        let input_ids_tensor =
277            tract_ndarray::Array2::from_shape_vec((1, seq_len), input_ids.to_vec()).map_err(
278                |e| SigError::Provider(format!("Failed to create input_ids tensor: {}", e)),
279            )?;
280
281        let attention_mask_tensor = tract_ndarray::Array2::from_shape_vec(
282            (1, seq_len),
283            attention_mask.to_vec(),
284        )
285        .map_err(|e| {
286            SigError::Provider(format!("Failed to create attention_mask tensor: {}", e))
287        })?;
288
289        // Create token_type_ids tensor (all zeros for single sentence input)
290        // BERT-based models require this third input even for single sentences
291        let token_type_ids: Vec<i64> = vec![0i64; seq_len];
292        let token_type_ids_tensor =
293            tract_ndarray::Array2::from_shape_vec((1, seq_len), token_type_ids).map_err(|e| {
294                SigError::Provider(format!("Failed to create token_type_ids tensor: {}", e))
295            })?;
296
297        // Convert to Tensor and run inference
298        let input_ids_value = Tensor::from(input_ids_tensor.into_dyn()).into();
299        let attention_mask_value = Tensor::from(attention_mask_tensor.into_dyn()).into();
300        let token_type_ids_value = Tensor::from(token_type_ids_tensor.into_dyn()).into();
301
302        let outputs = self
303            .model
304            .run(tvec!(
305                input_ids_value,
306                attention_mask_value,
307                token_type_ids_value
308            ))
309            .map_err(|e| SigError::Provider(format!("Model inference failed: {}", e)))?;
310
311        // Extract output tensor (last_hidden_state)
312        let output = outputs[0].to_array_view::<f32>().map_err(|e| {
313            SigError::Provider(format!("Failed to extract output tensor: {}", e))
314        })?;
315
316        // Convert to Array2 (batch_size=1, seq_len, hidden_dim)
317        let shape = output.shape();
318        if shape.len() != 3 || shape[0] != 1 {
319            return Err(SigError::Provider(format!(
320                "Unexpected output shape: {:?}",
321                shape
322            )));
323        }
324
325        let seq_len = shape[1];
326        let hidden_dim = shape[2];
327
328        // Remove batch dimension and convert to Array2
329        let output_2d = output
330            .index_axis(tract_ndarray::Axis(0), 0)
331            .to_owned()
332            .into_shape_with_order((seq_len, hidden_dim))
333            .map_err(|e| SigError::Provider(format!("Failed to reshape output: {}", e)))?;
334
335        Ok(output_2d)
336    }
337
338    /// Apply mean pooling to token embeddings.
339    ///
340    /// This averages token embeddings, weighted by the attention mask.
341    ///
342    /// # Arguments
343    ///
344    /// * `embeddings` - Token embeddings (seq_len x hidden_dim)
345    /// * `attention_mask` - Attention mask (seq_len)
346    ///
347    /// # Returns
348    ///
349    /// Pooled embedding vector (hidden_dim)
350    fn mean_pool(&self, embeddings: &Array2<f32>, attention_mask: &[i64]) -> Result<Vec<f32>> {
351        let (seq_len, hidden_dim) = embeddings.dim();
352
353        if seq_len != attention_mask.len() {
354            return Err(SigError::Provider(format!(
355                "Attention mask length ({}) does not match sequence length ({})",
356                attention_mask.len(),
357                seq_len
358            )));
359        }
360
361        let mut pooled = vec![0.0f32; hidden_dim];
362        let mut mask_sum = 0.0f32;
363
364        // Sum embeddings weighted by attention mask
365        for (i, &mask_val) in attention_mask.iter().enumerate() {
366            if mask_val == 1 {
367                let mask_f32 = mask_val as f32;
368                mask_sum += mask_f32;
369
370                for j in 0..hidden_dim {
371                    pooled[j] += embeddings[[i, j]] * mask_f32;
372                }
373            }
374        }
375
376        // Average
377        if mask_sum > 0.0 {
378            for val in &mut pooled {
379                *val /= mask_sum;
380            }
381        }
382
383        Ok(pooled)
384    }
385}
386
387#[async_trait]
388impl EmbeddingProvider for OnnxProvider {
389    fn name(&self) -> &str {
390        &self.name
391    }
392
393    fn model(&self) -> &str {
394        &self.model_name
395    }
396
397    fn dimensions(&self) -> usize {
398        self.dimensions
399    }
400
401    async fn generate_embedding(&self, text: &str) -> Result<EmbeddingResult> {
402        debug!("Generating embedding for text: {}", text);
403
404        // Tokenize
405        let (input_ids, attention_mask) = self.tokenize(text)?;
406        let token_count = input_ids.len();
407
408        // Run inference
409        let token_embeddings = self.run_inference(&input_ids, &attention_mask)?;
410
411        // Mean pooling
412        let embedding = self.mean_pool(&token_embeddings, &attention_mask)?;
413
414        // L2 normalization using the shared function
415        let normalized = normalize_vector(&embedding);
416        let sha256 = compute_embedding_sha256(&normalized);
417
418        debug!("Generated {}-dimensional embedding", embedding.len());
419
420        Ok(EmbeddingResult {
421            embedding,
422            normalized_embedding: normalized,
423            normalized_embedding_sha256: sha256,
424            model: self.model_name.clone(),
425            dimensions: self.dimensions,
426            token_count: Some(token_count),
427            timing_ms: None,
428        })
429    }
430
431    async fn close(&self) -> Result<()> {
432        debug!("Closing ONNX provider");
433        // tract doesn't require explicit cleanup
434        Ok(())
435    }
436}
